correctness.rationale: On the event every polygon side has >=1 sample, hull vertices are the endpoint-most samples on each side; missing region decomposes exactly into disjoint triangles with area (1/2)sin(theta_i) U_{i-1,+}U_{i,-}. Empty-side probability <=sum_i(1-l_i/L)^N, exponentially small. For any fixed endpoint thresholds the corresponding length L t_j/N arcs are disjoint for all sufficiently large N; joint survival (1-sum_j t_j/N)^N tends to exp(-sum_j t_j), establishing 2m independent unit-exponential limits. Each capped gap has tail <=e^-t on normalized scale, so Hölder and exponential empty-side bounds give moment convergence at every fixed integer order. Conditioning products gives Laplace transform prod_i∫ e^-x/(1+t c_i x)dx, moments k!sum_{sum j_i=k}prod_j(j_i!c_i^j_i); E= sum c_i; Var=3 sum c_i². Jensen on exterior angles φ_i=π-θ_i (sum 2π) and strict concavity of sin on (0,π) gives sharp equality iff equiangular. Independence and dimensionless normalization verified; positive fixed side lengths essential. Independently sampled product exponentials in square, equilateral triangle, regular pentagon support predicted means and variances; Monte Carlo cannot prove weak convergence or all moments.
residual_risks: No uniformity over degenerating polygons or nonfixed edge lengths.
